points: A leader should help repair the breaches: identify problems, offer solutions and guide people toward action, rather than only criticize or complain.
The fox exploits a broken wall for its own escape. Good leadership serves others instead of using a position for popularity, wealth or personal advantage.
Praise cannot replace repair. Positive reinforcement matters, but covering a weak wall with attractive plaster leaves the underlying problems to collapse in a storm.
Distorting Torah values can be harder to recognize than rejecting them openly. Religious language and symbols do not make a false message sound.
Leaders should comfort people who are suffering and challenge those who are complacent. The false prophets did the opposite: they pained the righteous and strengthened those doing wrong.
